_why: ADR 0168's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
ADR 0168 fixed a classifier that read 'no inhibitor involved' as a
request for the inhibitor model. A keyword now counts only where at
least one of its occurrences is not preceded by a negator.
N1 removes the negation check entirely -- the defect, restored.
N2 is the mutation that matters more. It makes the check too eager, by
scanning only the first occurrence of a keyword rather than every
occurrence. That passes every 'does not route a negated mention' test,
because those queries negate the only mention. It fails only on a query
that denies one thing and asserts another in the same sentence, which is
why such a test exists. The cheapest way to make a negation fix pass is
to over-apply it and start dropping real matches, and a table with only
N1 in it would not notice.
N3 empties the negator list to a single word. The original bug arrived
as 'no inhibitor' and 'without any inhibitors'; a fix covering only the
phrasings that were reported leaves the same defect under every synonym.
Not included, because no test here catches it: whether the negation
window is the right length. The four-word window is a judgement, the ADR
says so, and nothing in the suite would fail if it were three or five.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0168-negated-keywords.json
test: cd Science-Agent-Pipeline/artifacts/api-server && npx vitest run src/__tests__/negatedKeywords.test.ts src/__tests__/classifierEval.test.ts src/__tests__/llmAuthoredQueries.test.ts

mutations.description: the negation check is removed; any mention counts
mutations._note: The original defect. 'no inhibitor involved' routes to the inhibitor model again, and accuracy on the two affected fixtures falls by 2.6 and 2.8 points. Nothing errors -- the classifier just answers the question the student explicitly did not ask.

mutations.description: only the first occurrence of a keyword is checked for negation
mutations._note: The over-application failure. Every negated-mention test still passes, because in those queries the negated mention is the only one. A sentence that denies one thing and then asserts another silently loses the assertion. This is the mutation a table built only from the reported bug would miss.

mutations.description: the negator list shrinks to only the words the bug was reported with
mutations._note: Fixing the reported phrasings and no others. 'without an inhibitor' keeps working; 'in the absence of an inhibitor' and 'free of inhibitor' go back to selecting the inhibitor model.
